Rewrite a job from the current version of its template

Source: R/upgrade-job.R
upgrade_job.Rd

Upgrades one job: the file you name in path. It does not look for other jobs, so to upgrade several, call it once for each.

A job is a copy of its template as it stood on the day add_job wrote it. upgrade_job() writes the job again from the template as it stands now and carries the study's choices across, so a job keeps up with its template without re-entering every choice by hand.

Usage

upgrade_job(path, dir = NULL)

Arguments

path

The one job to upgrade: its .qmd file, relative to the working directory or absolute, such as "10_descriptive/dc.general.cohort.eda.qmd".

dir

Any directory in the study, used only to locate the study root. Defaults to the directory of path, which is right for any job inside its study.

Value

The upgraded job's path, invisibly. The report is written beside it.

Details

The template is read from the job's file name, in either spelling add_job has used. A study's choices are the top-level assignments to an upper-case name, such as DATASET <- "built", in the job's edit-* chunks. Each choice the current template also has replaces the template's assignment, its source text unchanged, multi-line values included. SUBJECT and TYPE are not carried: the file name owns them. Where the job had resolved a choice's EDIT: marker, the upgraded job drops the template's marker for it too.

Nothing is dropped silently. A choice the current template no longer has is written, commented out, at the end of the template's edit-study-choices chunk under a new EDIT: marker, so the job renders as a draft until someone decides. Prose and code outside the choices come from the current template, because without the template the job was copied from an analyst's edit cannot be told from the old template's text. The report lists every chunk that may hold such an edit.

The old job is kept beside the new one as <file>.pre-upgrade, a name nothing renders. The upgraded job takes the name add_job would give it today, so a job named before 2026-10 moves to the .-separated spelling. The report is written beside the job, with the .qmd extension replaced by -upgrade.md. It records the template, the package version, the old job's checksum, and the choices carried, not placed and new, with the chunks to review. It names choices and lines but never quotes their values, since a value can identify a patient. The upgrade refuses to overwrite any existing file.

Upgrading a job

Name the job's .qmd file. From the study root, a cohort EDA job is

upgrade_job("10_descriptive/dc.general.cohort.eda.qmd")

and several jobs are upgraded one call each:

for (job in c("10_descriptive/dc.general.cohort.eda.qmd",
              "10_descriptive/dc.general.cohort.gfup.qmd")) {
  upgrade_job(job)
}

You never name the template: the job's file name says which one it is. The job must sit inside its study; leave dir out unless you want to name a different directory of the same study.

Afterwards, render the job and read its report, <job>-upgrade.md, for the chunks to check. The old job is kept as <job>.pre-upgrade. Before upgrading the same job again, move both of those files aside: upgrade_job() never overwrites a file, so a second upgrade stops while either one is there.

See also

add_job, migrate_job

Examples

# \donttest{
root <- file.path(tempdir(), "upgrade-job-example")
invisible(hvtiRutilities::study_setup(root, "Example", 1L, renv = FALSE))
job <- add_job("dc", "cohort", "eda", dir = root, qualifier = "general")
# A study choice, made in the job.
lines <- readLines(job)
lines <- sub('^DATASET <- "built"', 'DATASET <- "built_r"', lines)
writeLines(lines, job)
upgraded <- upgrade_job(job)
grep("^DATASET <- ", readLines(upgraded), value = TRUE)
#> [1] "DATASET <- \"built_r\""
unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
# }
